request.prompt:
Job T02: usp_load_dim_policy (tsql), file estate/tsql/T02_usp_load_dim_policy.sql.
Policy dimension with type-2 history, loaded once per policy snapshot.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_policy
  3 |   Purpose  : Policy dimension for finance, actuarial and broker reporting. One
  4 |              row per version of a policy term, with its product, broker and
  5 |              customer segment. A new version starts whenever the status,
  6 |              broker, annual premium or vehicle registration changes from one
  7 |              policy snapshot to the next (type 2 history).
  8 |   Run by   : POL_SNAPSHOT_LOAD, once per policy snapshot, oldest first:
  9 |              EXEC dw.usp_load_dim_policy @SnapshotDate = '<snapshot date>'
 10 |   Output   : dw.dim_policy. Keeps history, so the procedure never truncates
 11 |              it. Deploying this script recreates the table empty: reload every
 12 |              snapshot in date order afterwards.
 13 |   Author   : MOB
 14 | 
 15 |   Change log
 16 |     2014-02-10  MOB   Initial version, one row per policy (CR-0655)
 17 |     2015-06-22  MOB   Broker name from the broker register (CR-0790)
 18 |     2016-09-05  TF    Direct business reported as broker DIRECT-SALES (CR-0961)
 19 |     2017-03-13  TF    Type 2 history with MERGE, surrogate key policy_sk
 20 |                       (CR-1077)
 21 |     2018-10-01  PH    Vehicle registration tracked for motor (CR-1388)
 22 |     2019-07-15  PH    Customer segment from dw.dim_customer (CR-1610)
 23 |     2020-02-03  TF    Refuse a snapshot older than the last one loaded
 24 |                       (INC-2105)
 25 |     2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
 26 | ==============================================================================*/
 27 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 28 | GO
 29 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_policy', N'U') IS NOT NULL
 30 |     DROP TABLE dw.dim_policy;
 31 | 
 32 | CREATE TABLE dw.dim_policy (
 33 |     policy_sk             INT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
 34 |     policy_id             INT            NOT NULL,
 35 |     policy_number         VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL,
 36 |     customer_id           INT            NOT NULL,
 37 |     customer_segment      CHAR(4)        NULL,
 38 |     product_code          VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
 39 |     product_name          NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
 40 |     lob_code              VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 41 |     broker_code           VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
 42 |     broker_name           NVARCHAR(80)   NULL,
 43 |     status                VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
 44 |     inception_date        DATE           NOT NULL,
 45 |     expiry_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
 46 |     cancellation_date     DATE           NULL,
 47 |     annual_premium        DECIMAL(12,2)  NOT NULL,
 48 |     currency              CHAR(3)        NOT NULL,
 49 |     vehicle_reg           VARCHAR(12)    NULL,
 50 |     ncd_years             INT            NULL,
 51 |     valid_from            DATE           NOT NULL,
 52 |     valid_to              DATE           NOT NULL,   -- 9999-12-31 while current
 53 |     is_current            CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,   -- Y / N
 54 |     source_snapshot_date  DATE           NOT NULL,
 55 |     load_ts               DATETIME2(3)   NOT NULL,
 56 |     CONSTRAINT pk_dim_policy PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (policy_sk)
 57 | );
 58 | 
 59 | CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX ix_dim_policy_policy_id ON dw.dim_policy (policy_id, is_current);
 60 | GO
 61 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_policy
 62 |     @SnapshotDate DATE
 63 | AS
 64 | BEGIN
 65 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 66 | 
 67 |     DECLARE @job_name     VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_policy',
 68 |             @rows         INT,
 69 |             @closed       INT,
 70 |             @last_loaded  DATE,
 71 |             @err_msg      NVARCHAR(4000),
 72 |             @err_no       INT;
 73 | 
 74 |     BEGIN TRY
 75 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 76 | 
 77 |         /* Oldest snapshot first: loading an older snapshot after a newer one
 78 |            would reopen versions that are already closed (INC-2105) */
 79 |         SELECT  @last_loaded = MAX(d.source_snapshot_date)
 80 |         FROM    dw.dim_policy d;
 81 | 
 82 |         IF @SnapshotDate < @last_loaded
 83 |             THROW 50001, 'dw.dim_policy already holds a later policy snapshot', 1;
 84 | 
 85 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#src') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #src;
 86 | 
 87 |         /* 1. This snapshot's policies with product, broker and customer segment */
 88 |         SELECT  p.policy_id,
 89 |                 p.policy_number,
 90 |                 p.customer_id,
 91 |                 c.segment_code                          AS customer_segment,
 92 |                 pr.product_code,
 93 |                 pr.product_name,
 94 |                 pr.lob_code,
 95 |                 ISNULL(p.broker_code, 'DIRECT-SALES')   AS broker_code,
 96 |                 b.broker_name,
 97 |                 p.status,
 98 |                 p.inception_date,
 99 |                 p.expiry_date,
100 |                 p.cancellation_date,
101 |                 p.annual_premium,
102 |                 p.currency,
103 |                 p.vehicle_reg,
104 |                 p.ncd_years
105 |         INTO    #src
106 |         FROM    stg.policy_snapshots p WITH (NOLOCK)
107 |         JOIN    stg.products pr WITH (NOLOCK)
108 |                 ON pr.product_code = p.product_code
109 |         LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK)
110 |                ON b.broker_code = p.broker_code
111 |         LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer c WITH (NOLOCK)
112 |                ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
113 |         WHERE   p.snapshot_date = @SnapshotDate;
114 | 
115 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
116 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'policy snapshot', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
117 | 
118 |         IF @rows = 0
119 |             THROW 50002, 'No policies found for this snapshot date', 1;
120 | 
121 |         CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX ix_src_policy_id ON #src (policy_id);
122 | 
123 |         BEGIN TRANSACTION;
124 | 
125 |         /* 2. Close the current version of policies whose status, broker, premium
126 |               or vehicle registration has changed since the last snapshot */
127 |         MERGE dw.dim_policy AS tgt
128 |         USING #src AS src
129 |            ON tgt.policy_id = src.policy_id
130 |           AND tgt.is_current = 'Y'
131 |         WHEN MATCHED AND (   ISNULL(src.status, '')        <> ISNULL(tgt.status, '')
132 |                           OR ISNULL(src.broker_code, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.broker_code, '')
133 |                           OR ISNULL(src.annual_premium, 0) <> ISNULL(tgt.annual_premium, 0)
134 |                           OR ISNULL(src.vehicle_reg, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.vehicle_reg, ''))
135 |         THEN UPDATE
136 |              SET    tgt.valid_to   = DATEADD(DAY, -1, @SnapshotDate),
137 |                     tgt.is_current = 'N';
138 | 
139 |         SET @closed = @@ROWCOUNT;
140 | 
141 |         /* 3. Open a current version for new policies and for those closed above */
142 |         INSERT INTO dw.dim_policy
143 |                (policy_id, policy_number, customer_id, customer_segment, product_code,
144 |                 product_name, lob_code, broker_code, broker_name, status, inception_date,
145 |                 expiry_date, cancellation_date, annual_premium, currency, vehicle_reg,
146 |                 ncd_years, valid_from, valid_to, is_current, source_snapshot_date, load_ts)
147 |         SELECT  s.policy_id, s.policy_number, s.customer_id, s.customer_segment, s.product_code,
148 |                 s.product_name, s.lob_code, s.broker_code, s.broker_name, s.status,
149 |                 s.inception_date, s.expiry_date, s.cancellation_date, s.annual_premium,
150 |                 s.currency, s.vehicle_reg, s.ncd_years,
151 |                 @SnapshotDate,
152 |                 '9999-12-31',
153 |                 'Y',
154 |                 @SnapshotDate,
155 |                 SYSDATETIME()
156 |         FROM    #src s
157 |         WHERE   NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
158 |                             FROM   dw.dim_policy d
159 |                             WHERE  d.policy_id = s.policy_id
160 |                               AND  d.is_current = 'Y')
161 |         ORDER BY s.policy_id;
162 | 
163 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
164 | 
165 |         COMMIT TRANSACTION;
166 | 
167 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions closed', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @closed;
168 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions opened', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
169 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
170 |     END TRY
171 |     BEGIN CATCH
172 |         IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
173 | 
174 |         SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
175 |                 @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();
176 | 
177 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
178 |              @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
179 |         THROW;
180 |     END CATCH
181 | END;
182 | GO

Trap cards:
- TSQL-01 (semantic) Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins. Legacy: Under a case-insensitive collation such as SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text compares equal regardless of letter case (and of trailing spaces, see TSQL-02): state = 'ACTIVE' also matches 'Active' and 'active'; GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and join keys put case variants together. The stored value is returned unchanged. Spark: Spark compares strings in binary order: 'Active' <> 'ACTIVE', so a filter drops case variants, a GROUP BY splits them into separate groups and a join misses them.
- TSQL-02 (semantic) Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces. Legacy: SQL Server pads the shorter string with spaces before comparing, so 'WEST ' = 'WEST' (also in IN, GROUP BY and joins). CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) values are stored and returned padded to n characters: 'AB' in a CHAR(4) column is 'AB '. LEN() ignores trailing spaces (TSQL-15). Leading spaces always count. Spark: Spark compares strings exactly, so 'WEST ' <> 'WEST', and its string type never pads. A value read from a CHAR source column keeps whatever spaces it was stored with.
- TSQL-03 (semantic) Integer division truncates. Legacy: INT / INT is integer division in T-SQL, truncating toward zero: 7 / 2 = 3, -7 / 2 = -3. The result type follows the operands, so the fraction is lost before any later cast, e.g. CAST(qty / pack_size AS DECIMAL(9,2)) or 100 * a / b. Spark: Spark's / always returns a double (7 / 2 = 3.5); DIV is integer division.
- TSQL-04 (semantic) DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, not elapsed periods. Legacy: DATEDIFF(datepart, a, b) counts the datepart boundaries crossed between a and b: DATEDIFF(year, '2025-12-31', '2026-01-01') = 1 and DATEDIFF(month, '2025-01-31', '2025-02-01') = 1. DATEDIFF(week, ...) counts Sundays crossed, whatever SET DATEFIRST says. DATEDIFF(day, ...) on DATE values equals the day difference. Spark: datediff(end, start) counts days (arguments reversed); months_between returns a fraction with its own month-end rule; floor(months/12) counts elapsed years, not boundaries.
- TSQL-05 (semantic) + concatenation with NULL yields NULL. Legacy: With CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL ON (the default), 'A' + NULL is NULL, so a whole concatenation is NULL when any part is. CONCAT() and CONCAT_WS() treat NULL as empty. Spark: Spark's + is arithmetic only; concat() returns NULL when any argument is NULL, while concat_ws() skips NULLs and format_string writes 'null'.
- TSQL-06 (semantic) ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks. Legacy: ISNULL(a, b) returns a's data type, so the replacement b is converted to it: a VARCHAR(5) column with ISNULL(col, 'UNKNOWN') returns 'UNKNO' (truncated), and ISNULL(int_col, 0.5) returns 0. COALESCE uses the highest-precedence type instead. Change detection written as ISNULL(src, '') <> ISNULL(tgt, '') treats NULL and '' as the same value. Spark: coalesce() keeps the replacement as written ('UNKNOWN') and widens types; it never truncates.
- TSQL-07 (semantic) DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values. Legacy: DECIMAL arithmetic follows fixed precision and scale rules (e.g. division keeps at least 6 decimal places, results are capped at 38 digits and the scale shrinks to fit); intermediate results are rounded at each step to their result type. ROUND(x, n) rounds half away from zero; ROUND(x, n, 1) truncates. Assigning to a DECIMAL(p,s) column rounds. Spark: Spark's decimal rules are similar but not identical (scale reduction, and doubles if an operand is a double literal); F.round on a double rounds the binary value, so a computed 2.675 (really 2.67499...) rounds to 2.67; bround is half-even.
- TSQL-08 (semantic) TOP and TOP WITH TIES. Legacy: TOP n returns n rows in ORDER BY order (arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is unique); TOP n WITH TIES also returns every row tied with the last one. Spark: limit(n) after orderBy returns exactly n rows; ties need a rank window.
- TSQL-09 (construct) CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY with TOP 1. Legacy: CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 ... WHERE inner.k = outer.k ORDER BY ...) picks one inner row per outer row and drops outer rows with no match; OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs. Spark: Spark has no APPLY; a lateral subquery or a window replaces it.
- TSQL-10 (construct) UPDATE ... FROM. Legacy: UPDATE t SET ... FROM t JOIN s ON ... updates each target row from one matching source row; with several matches, which one wins is undefined. Spark: DataFrames are immutable; an update becomes a join plus a select.
- TSQL-11 (construct) MERGE and type-2 history. Legacy: MERGE matches target and source rows and updates, inserts or deletes in one statement. Type-2 history closes the current version (valid_to, is_current) of changed rows and inserts a new current version; IDENTITY keys are assigned in the INSERT's ORDER BY order, continuing from the table's highest value. Spark: Spark has no MERGE on DataFrames (Delta MERGE exists for tables); the job must compute the new state as a whole table from the previous state and the batch.
- TSQL-12 (construct) Cursors and WHILE loops. Legacy: A cursor processes rows one at a time in its ORDER BY order; variables carry state between rows (running totals, last values). NULL arithmetic inside the loop propagates: SET @total = @total + NULL makes @total NULL for the rest of the loop. Spark: Spark is set-based; loops become aggregations or ordered windows.
- TSQL-13 (construct) Temp tables. Legacy: #temp tables hold intermediate results for the session. Spark: Intermediate results are DataFrames or temporary views.
- TSQL-14 (semantic) LIKE character classes. Legacy: T-SQL LIKE supports character classes: '[0-9]' matches one digit, '[A-Z]' one letter (case-insensitively under a CI collation), '[^0-9]' a non-digit; % and _ as usual. Spark: Spark's LIKE has only % and _; '[0-9]' matches the literal text '[0-9]'.
- TSQL-15 (semantic) LEN ignores trailing spaces; SUBSTRING from 0; LEFT and RIGHT. Legacy: LEN(x) does not count trailing spaces (DATALENGTH does). SUBSTRING(x, 0, n) returns n-1 characters, because position 0 is before the string. LEFT/RIGHT count characters. Spark: length() counts trailing spaces; substring(x, 0, n) is treated like position 1 and returns n characters.
- TSQL-16 (semantic) CONVERT style codes. Legacy: CONVERT(type, date, style) formats dates by style: 101 mm/dd/yyyy, 103 dd/mm/yyyy, 104 dd.mm.yyyy, 105 dd-mm-yyyy, 106 dd mon yyyy, 111 yyyy/mm/dd, 112 yyyymmdd, 120 yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss, 121 with milliseconds, 23 yyyy-mm-dd. Converting into a shorter CHAR(n)/VARCHAR(n) silently keeps the first n characters: CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) is yyyymm. Spark: A cast to string gives yyyy-MM-dd; date_format needs a Java pattern; nothing truncates.
- TSQL-17 (construct) PIVOT. Legacy: PIVOT (aggregate(value) FOR col IN ([a], [b])) groups by every other column of the source and turns listed values into columns; values not listed are dropped; missing combinations give NULL. Spark: groupBy(...).pivot(col, values).agg(...) does the same when the values are listed; the grouping columns must be stated explicitly.
- TSQL-18 (semantic) EOMONTH and DATEADD at month-end. Legacy: DATEADD(month, n, d) clamps to the last day of the target month: DATEADD(month, 1, '2024-01-31') = '2024-02-29'; adding months to an earlier date never moves to a month-end. EOMONTH(d, n) returns the last day of the month n months away. Spark: add_months clamps the same way but also moves a last-day-of-month input to the target month's last day (add_months('2024-02-29', 1) = '2024-03-31'); last_day(d) is EOMONTH.
- TSQL-19 (semantic) Text ordering under collations (accents, case) in ORDER BY, MIN, MAX and rankings. Legacy: Under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text sorts case-insensitively with accent rules (Á sorts with A); MIN/MAX on text and ORDER BY text in a ranking follow that order. Spark: Spark sorts strings by code point: 'Zoe' < 'aoife' and 'Á' sorts after 'Z'.

findings.note: ISNULL takes the type of p.broker_code, which is VARCHAR(10), so 'DIRECT-SALES' (12 chars) is cut to 'DIRECT-SAL'. A Spark coalesce would write the full literal.
The product join compares VARCHAR product_code values case-insensitively, so case variants still match. A Spark join drops them, and with them the policy row, because this is an inner join.
The product_code join ignores trailing spaces. In Spark, a code with trailing spaces fails the inner join and the policy is lost.

stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) and gets padded, while policy broker_code is VARCHAR(10). SQL Server ignores the padding when matching. In Spark the padded values do not match, so broker_name becomes NULL.
The broker join on text matches case variants under the CI collation. A Spark binary join misses them, so broker_name is NULL.
customer_segment is CHAR(4), copied from CHAR(4) segment_code, so legacy values are padded to 4 characters. Spark strings never pad, so shorter codes come out without trailing spaces.
The #src temp table holds the snapshot batch. In Spark it becomes a DataFrame or a temporary view.
This MERGE closes the current version of changed policies (valid_to = snapshot - 1, is_current = 'N'). Spark has to rebuild the whole dimension from its previous state and the batch.
The insert opens new current versions. The IDENTITY key policy_sk is assigned in policy_id order, continuing from the table's highest existing value, and Spark must reproduce that.
The status change check uses ISNULL(..., ''), so a NULL status and '' count as equal and no new version opens.
The status <> check is case-insensitive, so a change of letter case only (e.g. 'Active' to 'ACTIVE') opens no new version in legacy. Spark would open one.
The status <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a change in trailing spaces alone does not close the version in legacy.

The broker_code change check treats NULL and '' as the same value. Also, the source side has already been truncated to 'DIRECT-SAL' by the ISNULL at line 95, and Spark must compare against that truncated value.
The broker_code <> check is case-insensitive, so a broker code that changes only in letter case does not trigger a new version in legacy.
The broker_code <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a code that differs only by trailing spaces does not count as a change.
ISNULL(annual_premium, 0) treats a NULL premium and 0 as equal, so that difference opens no new version.
vehicle_reg is nullable. ISNULL(..., '') makes NULL and '' equal, so moving between NULL and empty opens no new version. Spark null-safe comparisons would treat it as a change.
The vehicle_reg <> check is case-insensitive, so a registration that changes only in case ('ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE') is not a change in legacy.
The vehicle_reg <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a registration with added trailing spaces is not seen as changed.
